review.notes: All 41 physical pages' extracted text was diffed line-wise against the OCR Markdown (case/punctuation normalized), plus a fence/heading structure scan (4 balanced code-fence pairs; no 4-backtick fences). Rendered verification at 300 dpi on physical pages 23, 27 and 39. The Chinese poem strings reported by the diff on pages 36-37 live inside the embedded Figure E.1/E.2 jpgs, so they are not reader-visible droppage. Chart/table numeric spot checks (Table 8 MSRL row, Table 9) match the print. Reference [89] OCR text 'ChartAssistant' versus printed 'ChartAssisstant' left unchanged: the double-s spelling is the PDF's own typo and source-faithful review keeps it out of patches.

patches.evidence: Rendered physical p.27 (CHAOS-Bench annotation, Appendix C) prints the example sentence with the perturbed word in italics: 'the word document can be modified into dacument.' The OCR normalized the deliberately perturbed nonsense word back to 'document', which destroys the annotation example's meaning; the render confirms the printed spelling is 'dacument'.

Rendered physical p.23 reference [71] (StrucTab) prints the author list '... Pengyuan Lyu, Huawen Shen, Xingyu Wan, ...' (line-wrapped after 'Huawen'); OCR misread the name as 'Huawei Shen'. Verified at 300 dpi.

patches.evidence: Rendered physical p.39 (Appendix E output example) shows the HunyuanOCR-1.5 output box printing the literal model-output line '### 近一年广州商品住宅供求量变化' followed by its markdown table; OCR promoted the line to a level-2 document heading that also contains the literal '###'. The patch removes only the spurious '## ' prefix so the heading text matches the printed output line.
